headline: Norway Protects 714 Square Miles of Arctic Marine Life
meta_description: Norway establishes Andfjorden Marine Protected Area, safeguarding whale populations, seabirds, and diverse ocean habitats across 714 square miles.
summary_short: Norway's new marine reserve spans 714 square miles, protecting coral reefs, kelp forests, whales, and seabirds while maintaining fishing and local cooperation.
body:
On September 18th, Norway designated a new marine protected area covering 714 square miles—nearly the size of 260,000 football pitches—in the northernmost waters between Nordland and Troms counties. Called the Andfjorden Marine Protected Area, this reserve shelters an extraordinary range of life: coral gardens, sponge communities, kelp forests, and abundant populations of fish, whales, and seabirds. The designation marks a watershed moment not because it locks humans out, but because it demonstrates how protection and use can coexist. Climate and Environment Minister Sigrun Aasland emphasized that the area "contributes both to our food supply and to unique nature experiences," and that restrictions will be stricter only in zones containing particularly vulnerable biodiversity.

The new reserve will be managed collaboratively by a board representing municipalities, county authorities, and the Sámi indigenous parliament—a structure that reflects local stakeholder involvement from the outset. This cooperative approach paid dividends during the designation process; Aasland specifically commended municipalities and fishing communities for their collaboration, calling it "excellent cooperation." The expansion increases Norway's protected marine territory from 4.8 to 6 percent of mainland territorial waters.

Andfjorden is the 24th area to be formally protected under Norway's Marine Protection Plan, which was established in 2004 with 36 candidate sites. The timing reflects a global momentum: marine reserves have recently been established in the Coral Triangle, around Papua New Guinea, Easter Island, and along Turkey's Mediterranean coast. Each designation represents a commitment that future generations will inherit not diminished but replenished seas—and in Norway's case, one where fishers, indigenous communities, and whales all have room to thrive.
quick_facts: September 18: Norway establishes Andfjorden Marine Protected Area
714 square miles of Arctic waters protected in Nordland and Troms
24 of 36 planned marine reserves now formally designated
Coral reefs, kelp forests, whales, and seabirds sheltered
Managed by board including Sámi indigenous parliament representatives
